summary.intent: Execute Phase 19.2 (IPFS upload performance optimization) gap closure, collect definitive three-point local baselines proving concurrent SDK pins and pebbleds datastore improvements, then merge the PR and begin staging deployment with a parallel IPFS datastore migration.
summary.outcome: Phase 19.2 gap closure plans executed and verified (6/6 must-haves), PR #342 merged with all 11 review threads resolved, staging deploy workflow triggered, and IPFS migration partially attempted before pivoting to a clean-slate approach with a learnings doc committed on a docs branch.

repo: SDK concurrent pins (`Promise.allSettled`) and pebbleds datastore are synergistic — concurrent pins alone cause a regression at 50 clients (p95 18.7s→44.7s, -26% throughput) because they double simultaneous Kubo write load; pebbleds handles the doubled load and restores+improves performance
At 75 clients, pebbleds eliminates failure mode entirely: 0 errors vs 10 on flatfs, p95 -53%, throughput +44%
Load test secrets (LOAD_TEST_SECRET, THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET) must be passed as inline shell env vars — vitest does not load dotenv, so .env files are ignored
Rate limiting is bypassed via X-Throttle-Bypass header (BypassableThrottlerGuard) — only active when NODE_ENV !== 'production'
DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL in apps/api/.env was pointing to localhost:3001 (mock-ipns-routing); someguy on 192.168.133.114:8190 is the correct target for staging-representative tests
Valid CIDs on staging are tracked in two tables: pinned_cids (file content) and folder_ipns where latest_cid IS NOT NULL — anything pinned on Kubo not in these tables is stale
Staging had 31,477 valid CIDs, 31,254 pinned on Kubo, only 1 stale CID — data was 99.997% clean
ipfs-ds-convert is archived and incompatible with modern Kubo (v0.40+) — there is no built-in datastore conversion command
The tag-staging-release workflow handles staging tagging properly — manual git tag pushes should not be used
CIDs in DB but not pinned on Kubo (~223 cases) are tolerated by the system — likely from failed uploads where DB record was created but pin didn't complete

code.finding: batchPublishIpnsRecords returns {totalSucceeded, totalFailed} — access totalFailed only if result.value exists (mock returns undefined in unit tests), emit ipns:batchPublishFailed typed event on failure consistent with share:reWrapFailed pattern
Shared test helpers extracted here: createTestConfig and setupFolder were duplicated identically across client.test.ts, client-extended.test.ts, and client-upload-concurrency.test.ts

New test file for concurrent pin orchestration — covers parallel execution, partial failure (one pin fails), and allSettled behavior. setTimeout(r, 10) replaced with Promise.resolve() for timer-free async flushing
ipns:batchPublishFailed added as typed SDK event for batch publish failures

workflow: Sequential ipfs pin add for 31K CIDs via bitswap is not viable — got stuck on first CID after minutes; parallel approach with xargs -P or dag export/import would be needed

Three-point local baseline comparison (no opts / SDK only / SDK+Kubo) in matched environment is more rigorous than staging vs localhost comparison — eliminates confounding variables and isolates each optimization's contribution
Concurrency probe (Run 0) before load test baselines is valuable — found throughput plateau at ~3.5 ops/s from 10+ clients, 50 clients was highest clean run on flatfs
pnpm dev started multiple times can leave zombie API processes — check PIDs and kill older ones; port 3000 can only be held by one process
When pushing a staging release, use the tag-staging-release workflow rather than manually tagging — the workflow handles proper release sequencing
For IPFS datastore migration on staging, clean slate is pragmatic given only 1 stale CID; ipfs dag export/import per CID is the right approach for production migration
CodeRabbit and GitHub Copilot reviews required 3 separate rounds of resolution (11 total threads) — batch fixes by round to minimize CI churn

Sequential ipfs pin add via bitswap overwhelmed the VPS and SSH connection dropped — 31K CIDs is too many for sequential pin migration
Background task for 100-client and 75-client probe runs timed out/failed with exit code 1 but results were already captured from earlier reads — stale task notifications caused confusion
Agent incorrectly pushed a manual git tag (staging-v0.26.6-rc-1) instead of triggering the tag-staging-release workflow — had to revert and re-trigger properly
SDK mock for batchPublishIpnsRecords returned undefined in unit tests after adding totalFailed check — required defensive access pattern
Duplicate API processes (3 pnpm dev instances running) caused transient DB health check failures during cleanup
ipfs-ds-convert is archived and unusable with modern Kubo — discovered mid-migration after already stopping the API and spinning up temp container
